chunks: As for what al-Ḥusayn ibn Saʿīd narrated from Faḍālah, from al-ʿAlāʾ, from Muḥammad, who said:
I asked him about a man who does not know whether he has prayed two rakʿahs or four. He said: “He repeats the salat (prayer).”
So this does not contradict the earlier reports, because this report is to be understood as referring to salat al-maghrib or al-ghadāh, in which doubt is not permitted, as we have explained.

Al-Shaykh, may Allah have mercy on him, said: If he doubts between two, three, and four, and his conjecture is balanced, he builds upon four, recites the tashahhud, and gives salām; then he prays two rakʿahs standing, recites the tashahhud, and gives salām; and he prays two rakʿahs sitting, in which he also recites the tashahhud and gives salām.

key_terms.الشَّكُّ: doubt regarding the performed number of rakʿahs
key_terms.الْغَدَاةِ: the morning prayer, meaning salat al-fajr
key_terms.بَنَى عَلَى الْأَرْبَعِ: he proceeds on the basis that the count is four
key_terms.تَشَهَّدَ وَسَلَّمَ: he recites the tashahhud and concludes with salām
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ جُلُوسٍ: two rakʿahs prayed sitting as precautionary prayer
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ مِنْ قِيَامٍ: two rakʿahs prayed standing as precautionary prayer
key_terms.صَلَاةِ الْمَغْرِبِ: the maghrib prayer, a prayer in which this kind of doubt has a distinct ruling
key_terms.يُعِيدُ الصَّلَاةَ: he repeats the salat (prayer) due to invalidating doubt

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a person doubts whether he prayed two, three, or four rakʿahs?
ai.summary: This passage addresses legal rulings concerning doubt in the number of rakʿahs during salat (prayer). It distinguishes between cases that require repeating the prayer and cases where one builds upon four and performs precautionary prayers, showing the detailed fiqh of forgetfulness and doubt in worship.
